newsitem.title: USA: US stock index futures end topsy-turvy day higher.
newsitem.headline: US stock index futures end topsy-turvy day higher.

text.p: U.S. stock index futures ended a topsy-turvy day higher due to the resiliency of the technology sector, traders and floor analysts said.
The ability of U.S. T-bond futures to trim losses into their close at 1400 CDT/1900 GMT also sparked buying in the Standard & Poor's 500 futures pit, they said.
September S&Ps rose to 958.60, above the all-time settlement high of 957.95. Traders said the market's intraday spikes to the upside occurred in light volume.
The Chicago Mercantile Exchange (CME) said Monday that S&P futures volume fell 20 percent in July 1997 from July 1996.
Regardless, traders look for September S&Ps to continue their ascent and test their all-time highs of 963.90 in the near-term.
September held above a support zone of 947.00 to 946.00 and gained upside momentum after cracking through the 953.00 area, they said. Buy-stop orders were hit between 953.00 and 953.30.
They pegged fair value for September S&Ps at 4.85 points above cash, with arbitrage buy programs at a premium of 5.90 points and arbitrage sell programs at a premium of 4.00 points.

September Nikkei futures remained lower, despite slightly oversold conditions, traders said. Expectations that September would test resistance at 19,840 were fueled when the contract traded at the minor resistance level of 19,780, they said.

At the end of pit trade, September S&Ps were up 2.40 at 955.40, KCBT Value Lines were up 1.70 at 842.70, new composites were 1.80 higher at 494.85, Nikkeis were down 120 at 19,760, Midcap 400s were 0.60 higher at 317.50, Russell 2000s were up 2.00 at 417.00 and Nasdaq 100s rose 12.75 at 1,131.50.
